claimVerdicts.independentSourceFamily: paper-level primary literature (peer-reviewed poison-control case series, JAPhA/PubMed 37392810, reported via independent secondary coverage)

notes: All four claims in this packet are fieldAuthorityRequired=true (regulatory/safety-critical/contraindication/compounding-warning), and all four now have at least one independent-family confirmation on top of their original DailyMed/FDA sourceRefs: NCBI Bookshelf/StatPearls (paper-level review) for the two indication claims and the MTC/MEN2 contraindication, and independent poison-control case-series literature for the compounded-product warning.

The packet's dailymed-ozempic, dailymed-wegovy, and fda-compounded-glp1-concerns sourceRefs all sit in the same 'regulator/label' family per the review taxonomy -- re-reading them, or fetching accessdata.fda.gov label PDFs, would NOT have counted as independent verification; StatPearls/NCBI Bookshelf and the SELECT-trial primary literature were used instead to satisfy the cross-family requirement.

The packet's own ops.reviewReasons ('Pilot regulatory evidence packet requires human review before publication') and reviewFlags ('verify latest label before publication') are satisfied by this review for the claims as currently worded; if the DailyMed label text is edited before publication, that specific edit should be re-diffed against the live label, since this review confirms substance, not byte-for-byte label text.

claimVerdicts.independentSourceFamily: independent clinical-reference summary of the black-box warning (distinct from the DailyMed label excerpts cited)
claimVerdicts.finding: Independent clinical-reference source corroborates the contraindication: tirzepatide carries an FDA black box warning for thyroid C-cell tumors, including medullary thyroid carcinoma, in patients with personal/family MTC history or MEN 2. claimVerdicts.independentSourceFamily: live FDA regulatory statement dated 2026-04-01 (materially updated/different regulator communication than the general 'FDA's Concerns with Unapproved GLP-1 Drugs' page cited, and cross-checked against independent trade/legal press: NCPA, Pharmacy Times, GoodRx)
claimVerdicts.finding: The packet's statement is generic ('FDA advises caution ... vigilant when prescribing compounded ... products') and understates the current regulatory posture. Independent verification against FDA's own later, more specific statement (issued 2026-04-01, per the directive's note that listings changed in April 2026) shows FDA has gone well past advising caution: it determined the tirzepatide shortage was resolved (Dec 19, 2024) and formally ENDED compounding enforcement discretion for tirzepatide — Feb 18, 2025 for 503A compounders and Mar 19, 2025 for 503B outsourcing facilities. Mass/routine compounding of tirzepatide as an 'essentially a copy' product is now generally NOT permitted absent documented patient-specific necessity (with a narrow ≤4-prescriptions/month enforcement-discretion allowance). The claim should be rewritten to state that FDA compounding discretion for tirzepatide has ended (with dates) rather than only 'advises caution,' since the current statement could mislead readers into thinking compounded tirzepatide remains a routinely FDA-tolerated option similar to during the shortage period.

claimVerdicts.independentSourceFamily: regulator/label (live FDA page re-check) + secondary legal/regulatory commentary
claimVerdicts.finding: The claim's sourceRef is the FDA bulk-substances page itself, so re-checking that same page live (a different visit, not the same cached read) plus an independent secondary confirmation was required. The LIVE FDA page today (fetched directly) does NOT list BPC-157 in the current Category 2 'significant safety risks' table; BPC-157 now appears only under 'Bulk drug substances nominated but withdrawn,' with the page's own modified-time metadata showing an April 22, 2026 update. An independent legal/regulatory-commentary source (Holt Law, corroborated by other industry blogs found in search) confirms FDA removed BPC-157 from Category 2 in April 2026 because the original nominators withdrew their nomination -- a procedural change, not new safety data -- and that FDA has scheduled a Pharmacy Compounding Advisory Committee session for July 23-24, 2026 to consider a path to approved compounding status. BPC-157 remains, in the interim, an unapproved new drug not on any approved compounding list ('regulatory limbo'), so the underlying caution is still directionally warranted, but the claim's present-tense statement ('FDA lists BPC-157 among bulk drug substances that may present significant safety risks') is now factually stale and should be rewritten to state that BPC-157 was removed from the Category 2 list in April 2026 following nomination withdrawal, remains unapproved/not on any permitted compounding list, and is subject to a pending July 2026 PCAC review -- rather than implying an active Category-2 listing.

claimVerdicts.independentSourceFamily: systematic review / paper-level primary literature (independent of the cited narrative literature-and-patent review), corroborated by structured-trial-registry information reported in journalism
claimVerdicts.finding: An independent systematic review (Vasireddi et al., 'Emerging Use of BPC-157 in Orthopaedic Sports Medicine,' PubMed 40756949, 2025) -- a different paper from the packet's cited narrative literature/patent review -- corroborates the scarcity of human evidence: of 36 studies reviewed, only 1 was a human clinical study (a small uncontrolled retrospective case series on intra-articular knee injections, 7/12 patients reporting improvement), and the authors state explicitly 'No clinical safety data were found' and only one registered Phase I trial exists with 'unknown status since 2016.' This independently confirms the packet's evidence-gap framing and adds a sharper, citable detail: there is not just a scarcity but essentially zero controlled human safety data, and the one existing registered trial has been dormant for a decade. Recommend adding this more specific detail (no clinical safety data found; sole registered trial's status unknown since 2016) as a strengthening addition rather than a correction.

claimVerdicts.independentSourceFamily: independent journalistic/professional-commentary source citing clinical and regulatory experts, materially different from the cited FDA page and PMC review
claimVerdicts.finding: STAT News (Feb 2026), an independent source not among the claim's sourceRefs, corroborates the exact pattern described: vendors and wellness influencers market BPC-157 as a transformative healing compound while a University of Utah Health physician is quoted stating it 'should not be used by humans' absent proper trials, nearly all evidence traces to one animal-research group, and a 2015 human trial was withdrawn from a public registry before external review with no peer-reviewed results ever published. A supplementary search of vendor/wellness pages (healingmaps, text2md, peptideadvisors, etc.) independently confirms the online 'proven healing peptide' framing the packet describes as needing misinformation labeling. One nuance: STAT's own regulatory framing (citing a 2023 FDA prohibition as current) is itself now stale per the April 2026 FDA update found for claim 1, which is a useful cross-check illustrating why the regulatory claim needs its own refresh, but does not undermine STAT's corroboration of the misinformation-gap claim itself.

promotionBlockers: Regulatory claim bpc157-regulatory-compounding-risk-001 (fieldAuthorityRequired=true) states FDA currently lists BPC-157 in the Category 2 significant-safety-risk compounding list; the live FDA page today shows BPC-157 was removed from that list in April 2026 (nomination withdrawn) and now sits under a 'withdrawn nomination' section pending a July 23-24, 2026 Pharmacy Compounding Advisory Committee review. This claim must be rewritten to reflect current status before the packet is promoted, since a stale regulatory-safety claim is exactly the kind of error the fieldAuthorityRequired gate exists to catch.

notes: Independent verification was performed per source-family rules: claim 1 was checked against a live (re-fetched) FDA page plus an independent legal/regulatory commentary source; claim 2 against a separate 2025 systematic review (different paper than the cited narrative review) with corroborating trial-registry detail; claim 3 against an independent STAT News investigative piece plus a spot-check of current vendor/wellness marketing pages.

No fabrication or unsalvageable sourcing was found -- the packet's underlying quotes and characterizations are accurate as of when it was likely compiled; the issue is temporal drift on the regulatory claim (FDA page changed April 2026), which is a normal, expected finding for a compounding-substance claim in this fast-moving regulatory area and is squarely what the review process is designed to catch.

claimVerdicts.independentSourceFamily: professional/compliance-body summary (anti-doping compliance organization, corroborated by a structured drugs.com WADA-list reproduction)
claimVerdicts.finding: Independent sources (BSCG anti-doping compliance blog; drugs.com's structured reproduction of the WADA list) both confirm thymosin beta-4/TB-500 is prohibited under WADA's peptide hormones/growth factors category, matching the claim's statement. Separately, the packet's regulatory coverage of TB-500 is WADA-only; an FDA Pharmacy Compounding Advisory Committee (PCAC) review in July 2026 reportedly recommended TB-500 for the 503A bulk drug substances compounding list (multiple industry/legal secondary sources; FDA's own advisory-committee page confirms the meeting occurred and TB-500 was on the agenda for 'wound healing' but its raw text does not itself state the vote outcome). claimVerdicts.independentSourceFamily: systematic/scoping review (MDPI, independent of the packet's cited Frontiers review)
claimVerdicts.finding: An independent scoping review (different review-family source than the packet's cited Frontiers 2021 article) strongly corroborates and sharpens this claim: of 80 papers reviewed, direct TB-500 human evidence was limited to a single study (in-vitro/metabolite profiling, not a clinical trial), and thymosin beta-4 (full protein) human evidence was concentrated in ocular/wound settings with no human interventional studies in tendon/ligament/muscle/bone/cartilage. This independently confirms the packet's caution against treating vendor TB-500 products as equivalent to studied thymosin beta-4 formulations.

claimVerdicts.independentSourceFamily: systematic/scoping review (MDPI, independent of the packet's cited Frontiers review)

This independently confirms the packet's framing that popular recovery/injury-repair claims for TB-500 outrun the human evidence and should remain an evidence-gap, not a proven-benefit claim.

promotionBlockers: Regulatory coverage is incomplete: the packet documents only WADA anti-doping status and is silent on the FDA Pharmacy Compounding Advisory Committee's July 2026 review/recommendation of TB-500 for the 503A bulk drug substances (compounding) list -- a significant, more recent regulatory development from an independent regulator-family source that should be added and fieldAuthorityRequired-flagged before public promotion.

notes: All 3 claims in the packet were independently verified against a source family materially different from their own sourceRefs, per the directive's Independent review rule.

The single fieldAuthorityRequired claim (WADA regulatory status) is confirmed-with-note by an independent professional/compliance-body source; no needs-adjustment or unresolved fieldAuthorityRequired claims remain, which supports approve-claims for the claims as currently written.

claimVerdicts.independentSourceFamily: controlled human study / clinical trial registry — materially different from the packet's systematic-review (PMC) citation

claimVerdicts.independentSourceFamily: regulator/label data (FDA 503A bulk drug substances nomination process) — materially different from the packet's review+database citations
claimVerdicts.finding: Live regulatory source (April 2026 FDA/PCAC update) confirms GHK-Cu has NO current FDA-sanctioned pathway for injectable/compounded use: it was removed from Category 1 nomination status after its nomination was withdrawn, with PCAC review of whether to add it to the 503A bulk drug substances list not scheduled until before February 2027. The packet's generic reviewFlag ('vendor injectable claims require misinformation monitoring') is directionally correct but two things need fixing: (1) this claim discusses injectable/regulatory boundary content and safety-relevant vendor claims, which per the extraction rules should be marked fieldAuthorityRequired=true — it currently is not, on any of the packet's three claims; (2) the claim should state the specific, current FDA/PCAC nomination status (not on the 503A bulks list; nomination withdrawn; PCAC review pending until ~Feb 2027) rather than leaving the regulatory gap implicit, since the directive requires regulatory content be checked against and reflect the live FDA record.

The regulatory status of GHK-Cu (no FDA drug approval; not currently on the 503A bulk drug substances list; nomination withdrawn with PCAC review pending until ~Feb 2027) is not stated anywhere in the packet, even though it directly bears on the packet's own misinformation-monitoring flag for injectable vendor claims.
